extracted.intended_audience: administrators, Title IX coordinators, and staff at K-12 and postsecondary educational institutions (recipients of federal funding)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recipients on obligations and procedures under final Title IX regulations relating to pregnancy and related conditions, including employee duties, Title IX Coordinator responsibilities, timelines, confidentiality, delegation, and grievance/remedy processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to provide Title IX Coordinator contact and other information
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the employee reasonably believes that the Title IX Coordinator has been notified of the student's pregnancy or related conditions, the employee's obligation is to promptly provide the student (or a person with legal right to act on their behalf) with the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and inform that person that the Title IX Coordinator can coordinate specific actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure the student's equal access to the education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employee need not ask whether the Title IX Coordinator has been notified; if unaware, the employee must provide the two required pieces of information. Example: if a student simply says 'I'm letting you know I'm pregnant,' the employee must give the Coordinator's contact info; but if the student says 'I'm pregnant and working with the Title IX Coordinator…' the employee may reasonably believe the Coordinator already knows and has no further obligation. A reasonable belief may also come from the Coordinator informing relevant staff. The Department favors erring on providing information to ensure student access while minimizing redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No documentation requirement for employee compliance under §106.40(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision does not require documentation of employee compliance with providing Title IX Coordinator contact information when a student notifies an employee of pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may voluntarily maintain records, but voluntary records are subject to disclosure restrictions under §106.44(j). The Department explicitly clarified there is no regulatory requirement to document an employee's act of informing a student under §106.40(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and disclosure restrictions (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any records maintained by a recipient in carrying out Title IX obligations regarding pregnancy or related conditions are subject to §106.44(j), which prohibits the disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with Title IX, with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator must inform the student (and legal representative, if applicable) of these disclosure restrictions when providing information under §106.40(b)(3)(i). The Department also reiterates that a recipient may not punish or retaliate against a student solely for seeking or obtaining an abortion; privacy protections and non-retaliation are integral to these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness of recipient actions under §106.40(b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Title IX Coordinator is notified of a student's pregnancy or related conditions, the recipient must promptly take the steps specified in §106.40(b)(3), including implementing reasonable modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of 'promptness' is fact-specific and depends on factors such as the needs of the student, the substance and timing of the requested modification, and characteristics of the education program or activity. Recipients are not required to implement modifications that they can demonstrate would 'fundamentally alter' the nature of the education program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student notice and recipient responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should encourage students to notify the Title IX Coordinator as early as possible, but regardless of when notification occurs the recipient must respond promptly and effectively to ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students may be unable or unwilling to provide advance notice for many reasons (e.g., sudden need, time to decide to disclose, lack of awareness). Many modifications can be implemented with relatively little administrative effort (e.g., allowing a student to sit/stand/drink during class). A student may return to the Coordinator for further needs and the recipient must take further action consistent with §106.40(b)(3)(ii)-(vi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing flexibility and coordination of actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is responsible for taking the actions required by §106.40(b)(3); the Title IX Coordinator must coordinate those actions, but may delegate duties to designees consistent with §106.8(a)(2), while retaining ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may assign other administrators or departments to carry out tasks, provided work is coordinated with the Title IX Coordinator and consistent with the final regulations. This flexibility helps manage workload but the Coordinator must ensure compliance. If a Coordinator has a conflict of interest or bias, they must be removed from investigatory/decisionmaking roles in a particular complaint per §106.45(b)(2). Coordinators must receive bias training as required by §106.8(d)(2)(iii) and (4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness requirement for recipient actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's actions under §106.40(b)(3) must be fully and effectively implemented and serve their intended purposes to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness requires ensuring all relevant staff comply with their roles and that no structural or resource barriers prevent implementation. Examples of ineffective implementation: providing a restroom accommodation but a teacher refuses to permit it; giving access codes to a lactation space but a broken keypad prevents entry. The recipient must remedy ineffective implementation to ensure access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to provide information about recipient obligations (§106.40(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notification of a student's pregnancy or related conditions, the Title IX Coordinator must inform the student (and legal representative, if applicable) of the recipient's obligations under §§106.40(b)(1)-(5) and §106.44(j), and provide the recipient's notice of nondiscrimination under §106.8(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information may be conveyed in a single conversation or, when age-appropriate, in a standardized written communication. The Department declined to limit or tailor the information required to be provided (e.g., excluding lactation when miscarriage) because broad disclosure empowers students to make informed choices and prevents staff misjudgment. While recipients may post procedure information on websites or syllabi, such general notices are not sufficient alone to ensure timely, individualized notice when a student notifies the Coordinator. Recipients may align pregnancy and disability procedures where consistent with Title IX and disability law, but must still satisfy §106.40(b)(3)(i) and Coordinator oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures, supportive measures, and remedies (application to pregnancy-related matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures under §106.45 (and §106.46, if applicable at postsecondary institutions) apply to pregnancy-related issues; if a student notifies the recipient of failure to implement a modification or lactation space, the recipient must take additional steps under §106.44(f)(1) to comply with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complaint alleges failure to implement required actions, use the recipient's grievance procedures to investigate and resolve; if sex discrimination is found, the Coordinator must coordinate provision and implementation of remedies per §106.45(h)(3). Supportive measures may also be required under §106.44(g) to restore or preserve access in the absence of a complaint or during grievance proceedings. Recipients with knowledge of possible sex discrimination must respond promptly and effectively under §106.44(a) and (f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee training requirement (§106.8(d)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must be trained to share two pieces of information when informed of a student's pregnancy or related conditions: (1) the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and (2) that the Title IX Coordinator can coordinate specific actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views the training burden as minimal; training can be incorporated into broader Title IX or other staff trainings and will likely require only a limited amount of time. See §106.8(d)(1)(iii) discussion for further explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of posting information on syllabi and websites (not a substitute for individualized notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may post information about availability of pregnancy-related modifications on syllabi or websites, but such non-directed notifications alone will not effectively ensure that students know about time-sensitive Title IX rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing prohibits posting such information, and recipients are welcome to do so, but individualized notification by the Coordinator upon student notice is required to ensure students receive timely, actionable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disciplining or penalizing pregnancy-related conduct (including abortion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not punish or retaliate against a student solely for seeking or obtaining an abortion; disciplining or referring students to law enforcement on pregnancy-related bases violates Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection is part of the Title IX obligations discussed in the §106.2 definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions' and is reiterated alongside confidentiality and nondiscrimination obligations. Recipients must ensure policies and staff practices do not result in civil/criminal penalties or retaliation for pregnancy-related conduct.
